issues: Whether the police had reasonable grounds (articulable cause) to detain the individual
Whether the street stop constituted an arbitrary detention under section 9 of the Charter
Whether the search of the individual violated section 8 of the Charter (unreasonable search and seizure)
Whether the evidence (drugs) should be excluded under section 24(2) of the Charter
Whether the detention and search were incidental to a lawful investigative purpose
Whether the accused's right to counsel under section 10(b) was engaged and complied with
key_facts: Police stopped the client on the street
Stop occurred with no real (articulated) grounds for suspicion
Client was questioned during the stop
Drugs were found on the client during or after the stop
causes_of_action: Challenge to unreasonable search and seizure (s. 8)
candidate_statutes: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
search_terms: R v Mann investigative detention test
needs_clarification: Which province/territory did this stop occur in, since this affects which court's precedents and any provincial policing regulations (e.g., street check rules) apply?
